_comment: Template for release_readiness.py init (issue #350). Do not put secrets in a readiness file.
Owner pc = the home PC loop does it. Owner hafiz or mac = a gate: listed, never done by the PC, closed by a person with evidence (pc_release.py gate).

Two measures: PC readiness counts applicable pc items. Prod readiness counts every applicable item that must close BEFORE the production deploy go (pc items plus the gates of the chosen route). Items with after_go true (deploy go, production smoke, monitoring, acceptance) are listed and never counted.
route is chosen per release at init: staging-first (items with route_only staging-first apply) or direct-prod (they are marked not applicable: Hafiz chose direct to production).

Tokens: <<name>> inside text and a whole-string @name are replaced at init (release, repo, branch, base, issue, github_repo, serving_commit, route, pr_numbers, suite_commands, e2e_commands, umbrella_script_dir). A whole-string @staging_sha is resolved when the check runs.
Items that do not apply are set to na with a reason at init (--na ITEM=reason, --e2e-exception).
Rules live in docs/agent-playbooks/release-deploy-live-monitoring.md and AGENTS.md 'Build, Evidence, And Release'.

items.title: Scope: what changes, who is affected, business-rule IDs, an acceptance example
items.instruction: Read the release diff, issue <<issue>> and, when the repo has a docs/business-rules folder, the rules the change touches. Name the applicable business-rule IDs with their one-line meaning and give one concrete acceptance example in the form: given this real situation, when this happens, then this result. If no rule applies, write 'none found' and say where you looked.

items.title: Release source: an open PR names the exact commit; built on the serving production commit when one is given
Cold review: an independent reviewer read the branch cold and said ACCEPT
items.instruction: Review the release branch against its base as a release candidate. Check the scope in release-pack/01-scope.md if it exists, a test that cannot fail, a rule broken, a claim without evidence, a file outside scope, anything that could expose a secret or act without approval, and (when the repo has them) the TESTING.md row and the RELEASE-DOCS.md decision for the changed behaviour.

items.title: Failing-first evidence: every new test fails on the base and passes on the release
items.instruction: A new or changed test must fail on the release base (with the release's test files copied onto it) and pass on the release. Strengthen the test so it fails without the change.

items.title: Suite: the project's own lint, type-check and unit tests pass on the PC
items.instruction: Make the failing commands pass without loosening a test or skipping a check.

items.title: Browser or E2E: specs updated and run where an app is available, otherwise a named exception
items.instruction: State which E2E or browser specs cover the changed behaviour and the exact command and exit code of the last run, or name one exception from AGENTS.md: missing credential, no safe representative data, destructive workflow, tooling unavailable, or not user-facing, with the reason. Do not claim a run you did not do.

items.title: Coverage and docs: the staff documentation decision is present (and the TESTING.md row when the project has one)
items.instruction: Add the release-documentation decision the check asks for, using the project's own RELEASE-DOCS.md format, or a concrete 'not relevant' reason.

items.title: Migration and rollback: migrations with rollback, or 'none'; flags and data changes; rollback steps
items.instruction: List every migration in the release diff with how to roll it back, or write 'Migrations: none'. List flags and data changes (or 'none'). Write rollback steps in order. Never run a migration.

items.title: Deploy plan: the exact commands per the project's deployment playbook, who runs each, in order
items.instruction: Read the project's deployment playbook and write the exact deploy commands in order and who runs each (Hafiz or the Mac session). Do not run any of them. For Ripple, base the plan on the serving commit in the deploy target's own record, and note the live-commit check from docs/agent-playbooks/release-deploy-live-monitoring.md. The route for this release is <<route>>: staging-first means staging is merged, deployed and smoke checked first (by Hafiz or a Mac session), then production; direct-prod means straight to production. Write the plan for this route only.

items.title: Smoke and monitoring plan: normal smoke, a change smoke per changed workflow, the monitoring window
items.instruction: Write the normal smoke, then a change smoke for every changed workflow with the role and login that will check it (never submit real data), then the monitoring window from the playbook table in docs/agent-playbooks/release-deploy-live-monitoring.md. The route for this release is <<route>>: staging-first means staging is merged, deployed and smoke checked first (by Hafiz or a Mac session), then production; direct-prod means straight to production. Write the plan for this route only.

items.title: Review page draft: business and technical explanation side by side, risks, evidence, required approvals
items.instruction: Draft the review page Hafiz confirms before any deploy. Business explanation and technical explanation side by side (two columns in a Markdown table). List the screenshots a person must still take (you cannot take them), the decisions, the risks, the evidence (commands with exit codes, PR numbers, job results in the release folder) and the approvals still required. The route for this release is <<route>>: staging-first means staging is merged, deployed and smoke checked first (by Hafiz or a Mac session), then production; direct-prod means straight to production. Write the plan for this route only.

items.title: Release notes draft
items.instruction: Write short release notes in plain language for the people the change affects, in the project's existing release-note style if it has one.

items.title: Release change merged into sifu-staging (or the project's staging branch)
Staging deployed, with the commit SHA as evidence (close with --sha)
Staging smoke checked: normal smoke plus change smoke per changed workflow
A promotion PR or release branch for the exact tested change exists for production
Route chosen by Hafiz, recorded with the date (init --route)
Review page confirmed by Hafiz
Migration or data approval (only when item 8 lists any)
Merge
Production deploy go (always Hafiz's)
Production smoke: normal smoke and change smoke
Production monitoring window checked
Accepted and closed
